lines.trans: Well? Did he shout? Did he ask for his money back?
Neither! He loved the quiet beams and thanked us.
Clara, you have a gift for hospitality! You saved my blood pressure!
He even finished every last drop of vegetable soup before going up.
Wait: whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Javier set it down there when he took the dry towel!
We must not snoop, of course... wait a moment, it fell open to the middle!
Why are there neat pencil drawings of three inns on our street?
Look at the words beside ours: Courtyard width, street noise, quiet score: nine out of ten!
Nine out of ten?! Nobody measures lobbies unless...
Unless he writes for the annual Valencia travel guide!
Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

Wait: whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

Neither! He loved the quiet beams and thanked us.
Clara, you have a gift for hospitality! You saved my blood pressure!
He even finished every last drop of vegetable soup before going up.

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: See you!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.
There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Measurement from side to side.

examples.text: La anchura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The width is very important here.
We talk about the width.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is an annual piece.

examples.text: ¡A menos que escriba para la guía anual de viajes de Valencia!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Valencia travel guide!

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Con calma means 'calmly / unhurriedly'.

examples.text: La calma es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The calm is very important here.
We talk about the calm.

cerrar.gloss: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)

meanings.en: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: cierro).

examples.text: Cierro la tienda a las ocho.
examples.trans: I close the shop at eight.
Last night we closed all the shutters.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.
Well of course you can come in!

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: De cuero = made of leather.

examples.text: El cuero es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The leather is very important here.
We talk about the leather.

meanings.note: Built from curioso.

examples.text: Nos gusta curiosear en el mercado viejo.
examples.trans: We like browsing around the old market.
He browsed curiously through the books on the shelf.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.
Everything works as it should.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

devolver.gloss: to return (an item); to give back

meanings.en: to return (an item); to give back
meanings.note: Conjugates like volver (o -> ue, past participle devuelto).

examples.text: Hoy devuelvo el libro a la biblioteca.
examples.trans: Today I am returning the book to the library.
We returned the key at the front desk.

meanings.note: Sketch or decorative pattern.

examples.trans: The drawing is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dibujos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drawings from the door.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Uncountable singular in Spanish.

examples.text: El dinero es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The money is very important here.
We talk about the money.

meanings.note: Respectful Spanish title used directly before a man's given name (don Ernesto).

examples.trans: The Mr / Sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mr / Sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Works like gustar: me encanta el té = I love tea (tea delights me).

examples.text: Me encanta el olor a pan caliente.
examples.trans: I love the smell of warm bread.

examples.text: De niño le encantaban los trenes.
examples.trans: As a boy he loved trains.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: De golpe = all of a sudden.

examples.trans: The knock is here.

examples.text: Vemos los golpes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the knocks from the door.

meanings.note: Ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.trans: The drop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las gotas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drops from the door.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Aquí nadie grita por las mañanas.
examples.trans: Nobody shouts here in the mornings.

examples.text: Gritó de alegría al ver a su hermana.
examples.trans: She shouted for joy on seeing her sister.

meanings.note: La guía de viajes = the travel guidebook.

examples.trans: The guidebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos las guías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guidebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Covers inns, hotels, and catering in Spain.

examples.text: La hostelería es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The hospitality trade is very important here.
We talk about the hospitality trade.

meanings.note: Adds an unexpected or emphatic item.

examples.text: Incluso el timbre estuvo callado hoy.
examples.trans: Even the buzzer stayed quiet today.
He works even on Sundays.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.trans: Sit next to the window.
We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: Plural marrones.

examples.trans: It is a brown piece.

examples.text: Dos pares de zapatos marrones de hombre y jerséis grises.
examples.trans: Two pairs of men's brown shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: mido, midió).

examples.text: Mido el ancho de la mesa nueva.
examples.trans: I measure the width of the new table.

examples.text: El carpintero midió la tabla dos veces.
examples.trans: The carpenter measured the plank twice.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: La persiana metálica = the metal shop shutter.

examples.trans: It is a metal piece.
Good! Is the metal shutter open?

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Reception desk or shop counter.

examples.trans: The counter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mostradores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the counters from the door.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.
We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Hacer ruido = make noise; hay ruido = it is noisy.

examples.trans: The noise is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ruidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noises from the door.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: ¡Salvados! = Saved!

examples.trans: It is a saved piece.

examples.text: Aquí están todas mis notas de la calle de esta semana. Me ha salvado.
examples.trans: All my street notes from this week are in here. You saved me.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Toallas secas = dry towels.

examples.trans: It is a dry piece.

examples.text: ¡Javier lo dejó ahí cuando cogió la toalla seca!
examples.trans: Javier set it down there when he took the dry towel!

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Plural tensiones.

examples.text: La tensión es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The tension is very important here.
We talk about the tension.

meanings.note: Clean bath or hand towel.

examples.trans: The towel is here.

examples.text: Vemos las toallas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the towels from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?
Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.
Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.
We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Sopa de verduras = vegetable soup.

examples.trans: The vegetable is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verduras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the vegetables from the door.

meanings.note: Hotel entrance hall.

examples.trans: The lobby is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vestíbulos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lobbys from the door.

meanings.note: Guía de viajes = travel guide.

examples.trans: The trip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viajes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trips from the door.

meanings.note: Vigas de madera = wooden roof beams.

examples.trans: The ceiling beam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vigas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceiling beams from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
